points: O generation of vipers, bring forth therefore fruits worthy of repentance, and begin not to say within yourselves, We have Abraham to our father.

note.label: Luke 3: The Preaching of John and the Generations Back to Adam

points: The generations run back through Nathan and David, through Judah, Jacob, Isaac and Abraham, through Sem and Noe, and to Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.

note.label: Luke 3: The Preaching of John and the Generations Back to Adam

points: Ought not this woman, being a daughter of Abraham, be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day? All his adversaries were ashamed, and all the people rejoiced.

note.label: Luke 13: Except Ye Repent, and the Strait Gate

points: They answered him, We be Abraham's seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free? We are not in slavery to anybody. I make six figures. I live in the suburbs. I make ten million dollars a year. I am a spokesman. I am a politician. I am no slave, Negro, you are a slave. I do well for myself. I can go where I want. I can do what I want. I have my amendment rights. In bondage to no man. So what do you mean, we are going to be free? We are already free.

note.label: Foundational Babylonian Advocates: Division Among the Dispersion

points: “They answered him, We be Abraham’s seed, and were never in bondage to any man: how sayest thou, Ye shall be made free?” So when the Pharisees heard it, they knew he was talking about captivity. They said, "We're not in bondage. We've never been in bondage to any man." Why did they say that? Because they were wealthy. They didn't see that Rome was over them taking taxes yearly; that's bondage. They didn't see it like that because they were living lively. That is that arrogant talk.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: Your father Abraham rejoiced to see my day: and he saw it, and was glad. That is a heavy sentence right there. You may ask when — that is for another class.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Then said the Jews unto him, Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham? This is what I want you to hear. They are telling Christ, you are not even an elder yet. Why? Because Christ was thirty.

note.label: When Children Walk in a Land of Shadows (Part 2)

points: Peter names "the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers," who glorified his Son Jesus, whom they delivered up and denied before Pilate when Pilate was determined to let him go. The oath and promise passed through a royal lineage: Abraham had Ishmael and the sons of Keturah, but Ishmael was rejected and Isaac was chosen.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: "Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed." The "ye" are the children of Israel, and "kindreds" means a lineage or family that descends from a common progenitor, Abraham, not all nations.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: This is Stephen at the council, addressing the audience just before he is put to death. He answers the high priest by going all the way back to the beginning: the God of glory appeared unto our father Abraham when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

points: Jacob went down into Egypt with threescore and fifteen souls, and he and our fathers died and were carried over into Sychem and laid in the sepulchre Abraham bought for a sum of money.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

points: As the time of the promise drew near which the Most High had sworn to Abraham, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt, until another king arose who knew not Joseph.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

points: Now, talking about the church. "What is the church? The church is anyone that believes in Jesus." Shut up, with your old black lips. “Saying, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.” The reason to start there: when they talk about the church fathers like Churchill and Martin Luther and all these stupid names they got, the fathers is what? The God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. That's the church fathers. That is the church fathers.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: What shall we say that Abraham our father, as pertaining to the flesh, hath found? All nations do not have Abraham as their father; our father means by ancestry, not by faith, so Paul is not writing to all nations. John 3:16, Galatians 3:28, Romans 11, and Acts 10 are conquered; Romans 5 is the last strong tower, and it has to come down.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: If Abraham were justified by works, he hath whereof to glory, but not before God; for what saith the scripture? Abraham believed God, and it was counted unto him for righteousness. Genesis 15: the Lord promised the old man an heir from his own bowels and seed as the stars, and he believed; promised him the land, and he believed; and only then was he told to take the heifer, the goat, the ram, and the birds and divide them. Faith came first, then the works.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walk Through of Romans 5

points: I say then, hath God cast away his people? God forbid. The answer is no. God has not cast away the 12 tribes of Israel. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. Once you read that on the street, that first verse tells you what the subject is about.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: With all this, they have something called Christian dispensationalism, or replacement theology: that God's people are done away with. I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid. Paul was dealing with that back then. For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin: Paul was proving the Israelites were not done away with.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: Even as Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him for righteousness. God promised him a son and land and seed as the sand of the sea, Abraham believed, and only afterward offered sacrifices; his faith came first and that was counted for righteousness, not the animal. They which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: Abraham believed God and it was accounted for righteousness: his faith came before his sacrificing, believing the land and the son in his old age. They which are of faith are the children of Abraham, and the heathen God justifies through faith are the scattered northern kingdom, covered last lesson.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Works Of The Law & Liberty

points: The scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, the Israelites scattered among the Gentiles, preached before the gospel unto Abraham: in thee shall all nations be blessed. See, brother, all nations. No: Esau already got his blessing, blood and death and slavery, weaponry, war, nukes, and witchcraft; he is dropping his blessings on Iran right now. Your blessing is to work, build up our kingdom, and survive the destruction as servants. They which be of faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree. The lynchings of our people from trees, lamps, and bridges were not coincidental. Christ nailed to a wooden cross hung by his hands and feet for hours: that is a lynching, and Christ died a black man's death. That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ, that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: If ye be Christ's, then are ye Abraham's seed, and heirs according to the promise. Romans 9:3-5: Paul's kinsmen according to the flesh, Israelites, to whom pertaineth the adoption, the glory, the covenants, the giving of the law, the service of God, and the promises, whose are the fathers, and of whom as concerning the flesh Christ came. The heirs are Israelites.

note.label: Navigating Through Paul's Letters: Walking Through Galatians

points: By faith Abraham, when he was called: Abraham was requested of God to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance. He obeyed, and obedience is an action; and he went out, not knowing whither he went, trusting in the Lord.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

points: Being in subjection unto their own husbands: even as Sara obeyed Abraham, calling him lord: whose daughters ye are, as long as ye do well, and are not afraid with any amazement. That you are not afraid to submit, that you are not afraid that those things will run you errant. How many of you have just been unyielding in certain situations. And yes, it does not make the things the husband might be doing right, but it does make you right if you stay in that lane with God. And then if you believe and you fear God and you have that confidence in him, then he will show you a path forward to have reconciliation in that division that is in your house.

note.label: SHE REVERENCE HER HUSBAND: Submission, Grace & Self-Examination of a Biblical Wife
